frequency_question: How often does the U.S. Department of Education or equivalent oversight bodies successfully carry out formal revocation of an established accrediting agency's recognition within a given decade?
membership_rule: Includes formal Department of Education reviews, restriction, probation, or termination proceedings against national or professional accrediting agencies. Excludes voluntary relinquishment of recognition or routine renewals without adverse enforcement action.

cases.name: Department of Education review and termination of ACICS recognition
ABA accreditation standards and Department of Education renewal friction
American Bar Association targeted review by National Advisory Committee on Institutional Quality and Integrity (NACIQI)

coverage_note: 3 major high-stakes review episodes identified; rare for full revocation to reach finality without settlement or reversal.
known_gaps: Excludes minor compliance warnings and informal secretarial advisories that did not reach formal revocation proceedings.
skeleton: Formal administrative challenges to accrediting agencies by the Department of Education per decade across the post-HEA (Higher Education Act) amendment era.
multiplier: 2 challenges per decade over 4 decades, with only 1 resulting in a complete termination of recognition.
validity_reason: Statutory frameworks under the Higher Education Act and administrative procedures governing recognition remain stable across multiple presidential administrations.
